notes: Perfect claim overlap (C47-C50) on directional control during gliding. LLM finds the force balance model well-demonstrated through biflagellate cell observations. Peer reviewers question the mechanism, noting the caption gives incorrect impression about flagellum lifting and that most reversals occur with both flagella in contact.

High overlap (7/8 claims: C20-C24, C84-C85) on FMG1-B bead colocalization with IFT trains. Both agree the evidence is convincing, with peer reviewers specifically noting pausing is 'abundantly clear and quite convincing in Video 2.' LLM includes additional claim C2 not addressed by peer review.

Perfect overlap (C75-C80) on viscous drag explanation. LLM finds the drag force calculations (16-24 pN) and viscosity measurements thoroughly convincing. Peer reviewers request clarification on whether observed viscosity is solely from membrane or includes motor-microtubule interactions, and question the mode of failure, suggesting additional experiments needed.

Strong overlap (12/15 claims) on dynein-1b as primary motor for gliding. Both accept the converging evidence from uniflagellate cells, temperature-sensitive mutants, and ciliobrevin D treatment. LLM includes additional claims C44-C45, C88 on mechanism details not specifically addressed in peer review.

Good overlap (8/17 claims: C3, C25-C30, C86) on IFT train pausing during gliding. Both find the pausing observations convincing, with peer reviewers noting it is 'abundantly clear.' LLM includes additional Ca2+ dependence claims (C51-C55, C93-C95) not in this peer review grouping.

Moderate overlap (8/16 claims: C51-C55, C93-C95) on Ca2+ dependence of IFT pausing. Both accept that Ca2+ is required for IFT train pausing and FMG1-B attachment. LLM includes additional claims on pausing observations (C3, C25-C30, C86) grouped separately in peer review.

Good overlap (7/10 claims: C5, C60-C62, C64-C66) on motor number estimates. Both accept optical trapping measurements (20-30 pN) and conclusion of at least four motors per IFT train. Peer reviewers request QPD signal clarification but don't challenge the force measurements or estimates.

Single claim overlap (C121) on motors not reaching maximum stall force. LLM rates this as uncertain, acknowledging it as speculation about motor coordination. Peer reviewers explicitly state this claim 'is not well supported by the data,' providing stronger negative assessment.

Perfect overlap (C6, C82-C83) on reciprocal motor coordination. Both accept that only one motor type is active at a time and that inhibiting dynein-1b reduces retrograde but not anterograde forces. No tug-of-war between motors.

Partial overlap (C81, C83, C100) on reciprocal coordination and lack of tug-of-war. Both accept the temperature-shift experiments showing motors don't engage in tug-of-war. LLM includes additional claims (C39-C41, C125) on kinesin inhibitory role not in this peer grouping.

Moderate overlap (C72-C74, C90) on viscous drag slowing IFT trains. Both accept that beads slow IFT trains and this explains gliding speed differences. Peer review questions relate to methodology clarification rather than challenging observations.

Perfect overlap (C69-C71) on control experiments. Both accept that forces remain constant across antibody coating conditions, ruling out clustering artifacts, and that asymmetry in escape events is consistent with FMG1-B biology.

Small overlap (C56-C57) on Ca2+ regulating FMG1-B attachment rather than motor activation. Both accept the observation that beads diffuse but don't move processively in Ca2+-deprived cells. LLM includes additional mechanistic reasoning (C91-C92) not explicitly in peer grouping.

Small overlap (C45, C88) on core mechanism that gliding is powered by IFT machinery with dynein motors pulling when surface-tethered. Both accept this central conclusion. Peer review notes article was 'favorably evaluated' and doesn't question this mechanism.
Claims C128-C129 on short lag time between IFT pausing and gliding initiation only appear in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this temporal analysis.
Claims C105-C106, C110 on speculative roles of IFT in mating and cell-cell adhesion only appear in LLM results. These are extrapolations lacking direct experimental support in the study.
Claims C67-C68 on multiple motors enhancing processivity only appear in LLM results. LLM notes these are reasonable but not directly tested speculations.
Claim C59 on Ca2+ signaling controlling directionality and timing only appears in LLM results. LLM rates as speculative since specific signaling mechanisms remain to be demonstrated.
Claims C96-C97 on FMG1-B dephosphorylation and GAK regulation only appear in LLM results. These are cited from prior literature but not directly investigated in current study.
